pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: New Jersey journeyman electrician preparation should include the National Electrical Code, electrical theory, practical installation knowledge, conductor sizing, grounding and bonding, services, feeders, branch circuits, motors, transformers, wiring methods, raceways, boxes, overcurrent protection, special occupancies, special equipment, safety, and calculations. Candidates should also be prepared to review New Jersey electrical laws, board rules, permit-related responsibilities, and state-specific requirements when those topics are part of the exam or credential path. Electrical calculations are an important part of journeyman-level preparation. Candidates should practice service load calculations, feeder calculations, branch-circuit calculations, conductor ampacity, conductor adjustment and correction, voltage drop, box fill, raceway fill, motor calculations, transformer calculations, demand factors, neutral loads, continuous loads, and overcurrent protection sizing. Calculation questions can be challenging under time pressure, so repeated practice is a key part of preparation.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The New Jersey Electrical Contractors Licensing Examination is administered through PSI after the applicant receives authorization from the New Jersey Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors. Candidates must complete the Board’s application process and submit required documentation before receiving approval to test. PSI administers the computer-based examination after the Board determines that the candidate is eligible. The New Jersey electrical contractor licensing exam includes an electrical contracting trade portion and a business and law portion. The electrical contracting portion focuses on code knowledge, installation requirements, electrical theory, and practical trade application. The business and law portion focuses on the business, legal, and regulatory responsibilities connected to operating as a licensed electrical contractor in New Jersey. New Jersey electrical contractor applicants must meet the experience and qualification requirements set by the Board.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The New Jersey Electrical Contractors Licensing Examination is an open-book examination. Open-book testing still requires serious preparation because candidates must know where to look, how to read the rule, and how to apply it correctly within the time allowed. A candidate who is not comfortable using the NEC can spend too much time searching and lose focus during the exam. An open-book electrical exam does not mean the answers are easy to find. Questions may require candidates to connect multiple sections, understand definitions, apply table notes, recognize exceptions, complete calculations, and compare answer choices against the wording of the code. Strong preparation includes practicing with the code book as a working reference, not simply reading it from front to back. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs supports this part of preparation. Tabs help candidates become more familiar with the layout of the NEC, including chapters, articles, tables, definitions, and major subject areas.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: The New Jersey electrical licensing process begins with identifying the correct credential. Candidates pursuing electrical contracting in New Jersey should review the electrical contractor license requirements through the New Jersey Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors. Candidates pursuing qualified journeyman electrician registration should review the registration requirements that apply to that credential. The electrical contractor licensing path requires submission of the required application forms, work experience certification forms, and supporting documentation. The Board reviews the application and determines whether the candidate is eligible to sit for the examination. pieces.h: State Requirements

Candidates should follow the state process rather than relying on a local-only license path for electrical contractor licensure.
